_provenance.what: The ARC-3 human replays this project owns directly, as opposed to the ones it harvested from a public page. Each row is the run metadata its /api/sessions/<guid> document reports. Sibling file published-replays.json holds the blog-linked set; the two are deliberately NOT merged.
_provenance.why: published-replays.json's provenance is exactly 'linked from the ARC blog post', and that claim is only worth something if every row in the file satisfies it. These three replays do not: they were played on our side and are not in the blog's 250. Folding them in would have made the larger file's one-line provenance false for three rows, so they live here instead. Plan docs/trace-findings/2026-09-14-decision-step-corpus-v0-plan.md §5 step 3 is what pulls recordings; this file records which guids are ours to pull.
_provenance.collected: 2026-09-15, one /api/sessions request per guid via tools/replay_scrape.py's fetch_session(). Every field below was fetched, not transcribed from a chat message or a doc.

caveats: Three rows is not a corpus. All three are WINs, which is what the decision-step record wants, but they are three correlated human sessions on three different environments — one win per game, no second run to cross-check a segmentation against.

'First-party' here means 'this project pulled it directly', not 'the Boss played all of it'. Only the cd82 row has a named player; see attribution. The other two carry tags: ['human'] and nothing finer.
These three are absent from published-replays.json and that is the invariant worth preserving: the two files must stay disjoint by guid. scripts/test_decision_step_validator.py asserts it.

Row shape is kept byte-identical to published-replays.json's rows minus blog_link_text, which is an artifact of the blog table and would be meaningless here. /api/sessions also serves score, card_id, tags and source_url; those are deliberately not stored, because the sibling file does not store them either and one row shape is easier to trust than two.

cd82-fb555c5d is a game the rest of the corpus tooling has never seen. Its recording pulled clean at 217 rows / 10,487,262 bytes on 2026-09-15 and its rows carry the same data.frame shape (a list of 64x64 grids) the SCHEMA.md frame convention assumes — but no fixture cites it yet.

fields.game_id: from /api/sessions environments[].runs[].id — needed to build the recordings URL
fields.actions: total actions in the run, from /api/sessions
